title: AI-Generated Code Is Already Competing With Human Code — Daksh Gupta, Greptile
talk_summary: Greptile co-founder Daksh Gupta analyzed over a million monthly PRs to test whether fully AI-generated PRs are worse than human ones, finding roughly equal revert rates, bug-finding rates, and review-iteration counts, but distinct failure-mode profiles per agent. He then reframes code review around three questions (user-contract violation, future-violation risk, intent fulfillment) and reports that ~20% of Greptile-reviewed PRs now merge with no human review.

takeaways.technique: Measure review recall with outcome proxies (revert rate, review-round count) instead of trusting reviewer scores
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat revert rate and number of review cycles before merge as ground-truth quality signals, then compare agents vs humans on those outcomes rather than on reviewer opinion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Codex PR is reverted about one out of every thousand poll requests... Humans right in the middle at about two and a half.
takeaways.numbers: Revert rates: Codex ~1/1000, Devin ~3.5/1000, humans ~2.5/1000; review cycles to merge: Devin 2.1, Codex 2.45, humans in between

takeaways.technique: Per-model failure-mode profiling from review comments
takeaways.what_they_do: They scan millions of review comments for specific defect phrases (SQL injection, N+1 query, auth bypass) and plot each agent's propensity relative to humans, revealing that different models fail in different ways.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Claude is one and a half times more likely to produce a SQL injection error than humans. Devon is about half as likely as humans to produce a off bypass issue.
takeaways.numbers: Claude 1.5x human rate of SQL-injection findings; Devin ~0.5x on auth bypass

takeaways.technique: Three-question review rubric (contract violation, future-risk, intent match)
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of 'automate code review', they define validation as answering: does this change violate the user contract, does it increase propensity of future violation, and does it fulfill the author's stated intent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: does this change violate the user contract? ... does it increase the propensity of a future violation ... does it fulfill the intent that the author described?

takeaways.technique: Sandboxed runtime validation: install deps, boot app, drive browser/mock inputs
takeaways.what_they_do: Their review agents spin up the changed code in a sandbox, install dependencies, start localhost, and click around / mock inputs to actually break the app rather than only reading the diff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it also spins up your code in a sandbox, installs the dependencies, spins up local host, clicks around to try to break things, mocks inputs

takeaways.technique: Swarm review over changed files plus related files
takeaways.what_they_do: A swarm of agents reviews every changed file and every file related to the changed files to find bugs, giving context beyond the diff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a swarm of agents and they go and look at every file that's changed, every file that's related to the files that changed

takeaways.technique: Design validation for high PR throughput (P90/P99 authors)
takeaways.what_they_do: They note median users write ~50 PRs/month but P90 writes 500 and P99 thousands, and argue existing manual review/QA cannot scale, motivating automated validation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The median grubile user writes 50 pull requests a month... The 90th percentile writes 500 poll requests per month.
